page_title: Graph-Theoretic Neural Network Fragmentation with Covariant Direct Molecular Force Learning: Enabling Coupled-Cluster Accuracy AIMD for Fluxional Systems
subject: graph-theoretic molecular fragmentation
statement: The paper presents a graph-theoretic molecular fragmentation framework integrated with machine learning to directly model post-Hartree-Fock nuclear forces at coupled cluster accuracy.

page_title: Graph-Theoretic Neural Network Fragmentation with Covariant Direct Molecular Force Learning: Enabling Coupled-Cluster Accuracy AIMD for Fluxional Systems
subject: graph-theoretic molecular fragmentation
statement: The paper achieves exceptional parameter efficiency through a vector-valued training protocol that reduces trainable parameters by over an order of magnitude.

page_title: Graph-Theoretic Neural Network Fragmentation with Covariant Direct Molecular Force Learning: Enabling Coupled-Cluster Accuracy AIMD for Fluxional Systems
subject: graph-theoretic molecular fragmentation
statement: The paper uses an unsupervised mini-batch k-means space tessellation algorithm to construct highly representative training databases using only 10% to 20% of reference configurations.

page_title: Graph-Theoretic Neural Network Fragmentation with Covariant Direct Molecular Force Learning: Enabling Coupled-Cluster Accuracy AIMD for Fluxional Systems
subject: graph-theoretic molecular fragmentation
statement: The paper validates the framework on the solvated Zundel cation (H13O6+), with fully machine-learning-predicted AIMD trajectories successfully reproducing complex dynamical signatures, radial distribution functions, and velocity autocorrelation power spectra.

page_title: An Insight on Evaluation Metrics Under the Imbalanced Case of Anomaly Detection
subject: metric landscape
statement: The paper introduces metric landscapes, visualizations that relate metric values to true positive and true negative rates, providing an intuitive view of metric preferences and stability under imbalance.

page_title: An Insight on Evaluation Metrics Under the Imbalanced Case of Anomaly Detection
subject: metric landscape
statement: The paper shows that anomaly detection metrics such as AUROC, AUPR, F1-score, and MCC convey different meanings depending on the anomaly ratio.

page_title: An Insight on Evaluation Metrics Under the Imbalanced Case of Anomaly Detection
subject: metric landscape
statement: The paper provides practical guidance for interpreting and comparing anomaly detection results across datasets with different imbalance ratios.

page_title: A Roadmap to Impactful Pluralistic Alignment Research
subject: pluralistic alignment
statement: The paper finds no public evidence that pluralistic alignment research has shaped the training or evaluation of frontier AI systems, with frontier labs not naming pluralism as an explicit goal.

page_title: A Roadmap to Impactful Pluralistic Alignment Research
subject: pluralistic alignment
statement: The paper identifies that pluralistic alignment justifications have been normative or speculative, and calls for studies empirically demonstrating how pluralistic AI benefits users or society.

page_title: A Roadmap to Impactful Pluralistic Alignment Research
subject: pluralistic alignment
statement: The paper argues that the pluralistic alignment community has not established when pluralistic behavior is warranted or what pluralism should look like in practice, requiring a concrete goal for developers.

page_title: A Roadmap to Impactful Pluralistic Alignment Research
subject: pluralistic alignment
statement: The paper reports that current pluralistic alignment methods trade off against other LLM desiderata in ways that are largely unmeasured, requiring trade-off-aware evaluations and methods built for production systems.

page_title: The Prompt Is Not the Query: How Request State Evolves Across Multi-Turn AI Conversations
subject: conversation-conditioned request state
statement: The paper introduces conversation-conditioned request state as an observable construct to replace latent intent, measuring how request state is distributed across user turns.

page_title: The Prompt Is Not the Query: How Request State Evolves Across Multi-Turn AI Conversations
subject: conversation-conditioned request state
statement: The paper reports that the final prompt in commercial multi-turn conversations contains a median 35.6% of the session's unique user-side content vocabulary, and 36.4% in PRISM conversations.

page_title: The Prompt Is Not the Query: How Request State Evolves Across Multi-Turn AI Conversations
subject: conversation-conditioned request state
statement: The paper finds that transparent rules detect at least one request-state dimension in history but not in the final prompt in 50.3% of commercial conversations and 44.8% of PRISM conversations.

page_title: The Prompt Is Not the Query: How Request State Evolves Across Multi-Turn AI Conversations
subject: conversation-conditioned request state
statement: The paper shows that among dimension-bearing conversations, the final prompt reproduces the full observed dimension set in only 26.1% (commercial) and 26.2% (PRISM) of cases.

page_title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
subject: epistemic mediation
statement: The paper reports that Grok's Fast versions assigned credibility scores of 70-75 to ethnonationalist pseudo-science, two to five times higher than Claude, GPT, and Gemini which scored 15-40.

page_title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
subject: epistemic mediation
statement: The paper finds this high-credibility pattern for pseudo-science absent from control prompts testing basic evolutionary consensus and refuted Lamarckian claims, where all models performed comparably.

page_title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
subject: epistemic mediation
statement: The paper documents that a silent patch reversed Grok's behavior from chaotic to stably high validation overnight, without any public documentation.

page_title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
subject: epistemic mediation
statement: The paper reports that the same Grok model identifier produced radically divergent outputs via API (score 75) and web interface (score 5.5) three months later.

page_title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
subject: epistemic mediation
statement: The paper observes that refusal to rate the pseudo-scientific claim appeared in Claude Opus 4.1 categorically via web and GPT-5.1 Chat intermittently via API, but eroded in successor versions of each model.
